definitions.explanation: An interactive educational session where participants actively learn through hands-on activities, discussions, and group work rather than passive listening.
A workplace for artists, craftspeople, or makers to create their works, often also used for teaching.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: From English "workshop." Often abbreviated as WS in Japanese.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ワークショップ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開催|かいさい}する→開催する：10441_kaisaisuru⟧ (to hold a workshop)
- ワークショップ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参加|さんか}する→参加する：25408_sankasuru⟧ (to participate in a workshop)
- ワークショップ⟦{形式|けいしき}→形式：00211_keishiki⟧ (workshop format)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ワークショップ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}く→開く：01979_hiraku⟧ (to hold a workshop)
- ワークショップ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{講師|こうし}→講師：00451_koushi⟧ (workshop instructor/facilitator)
- ⟦{親子|おやこ}→親子：10430_oyako⟧ワークショップ (parent-child workshop)
- ⟦{体験|たいけん}→体験：11443_taiken⟧ワークショップ (hands-on workshop)
- ⟦{企業|きぎょう}→企業：00225_kigyou⟧⟦{研修|けんしゅう}→研修：05322_kenshuu⟧ワークショップ (corporate training workshop)

DIFFERENCE FROM OTHER TERMS:
- ⟦{講義|こうぎ}→講義：01579_kougi⟧ - lecture (one-way, passive)
- ⟦{研修|けんしゅう}→研修：05322_kenshuu⟧ - training (formal, company-organized)
- ⟦セミナー→セミナー：11000_seminaa⟧ - seminar (may or may not be interactive)
- ワークショップ - workshop (always interactive and participatory)

CONTEXT: Widely used in education, business training, arts, community building, and design thinking. The emphasis on participation and hands-on learning distinguishes it from traditional lectures.
